samples.text: The current position is a manual one. The interim measure in place is this: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. It was chosen because waiting for a permanent fix would hold the period open for longer than finance can accept. The basis for the override is the confirmed diagnosis. The failure traces to stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Engineers therefore know which entries to correct, and the override replaces those entries only for this run. It does not alter the register itself, and the same stale rows will be read again on the next scheduled batch. For readers deciding whether to wait, the answer is that the period does not need to wait. The override gives a usable result now, based on a cause that has been confirmed rather than guessed. The risk sits in the next cycle. A hand correction carries no lasting protection, so the register still needs a proper repair before the following month end. Until

The inventory valuation service failed because the agency code mapping it reads was out of date. The confirmed cause is stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Legacy and cloud agency codes are both still in use and are not interchangeable. A stale row in that table therefore sends a valuation lookup to a code that the cloud platform does not recognise. Our first working explanation was different. The incident record initially gave the cause as overnight ERP outage, and the team worked on that basis during the first hours. That hypothesis was ruled out on evidence: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the upstream system cleared, the investigation moved to the reference data, where the stale mapping was found. Review has since classified the root cause as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer.
